Team — forwarded the ask from Quantacore. High level strategy I recommend before we send a formal counter: 

1) Commercial structure (aim for: protect customer while preserving unit economics):
   - 3-month price hold at current effective rate (October–December)
   - Burst pool capacity: up to 40% above baseline; overage billed at a 10% premium but we apply a one-time credit equal to 5% of the overage if actuals are within forecast band
   - If Quantacore converts the burst into a 12-month higher commit within 30 days after spike window, apply a 3% conversion credit across the newly committed volume

2) Alternative: shorter protection (6 weeks) + larger conversion credit if they commit earlier — use if finance needs tighter guardrails

3) Ask Legal to prepare a slim SOW amendment + DocuSign-ready term sheet. We should avoid multi-page legal redlines in this phase.

Numbers: I need Ben to run likely margin impact and a proposed % discount ladder across commit bands. Priyom — prepare a quick sample invoice schedule and final payment terms (net 30/45 discussion).

Goal: get a signed amendment or DocuSign by Oct 12 to meet procurement.

Thanks — Evelyn

Evelyn — ran a quick sensitivity. High level: the proposed approach works but we should tighten the overage credit mechanics to reduce downside. Notes:

- If we offer 10% premium on overage and give 5% one-time credit back, expected net uplift is small but predictable. I recommend reducing the credit to 3% and introducing usage bands: 0-20% overage (no credit), 20-40% overage (3% credit), >40% (no credit, escalate to exec).
- Impact to ARR (12-month run rate scenario if they convert) is +12% ARR; short-term margin pressure in Q4 ~ -1.8% absolute. Acceptable if we get conversion commitment.
- Require procurement to accept a one-time true-up invoice after the 3-month window that reconciles burst usage; recommend Net45 for that invoice.

I'll prepare a quick spreadsheet with banded pricing for Marissa to present. Ben

Rajiv — thanks for the data and the quick call earlier. We've drafted a compact amendment that should meet procurement timelines and give Quantacore the runway you asked for. Summary of the counterproposal: 

- 3-month price hold (Oct 1 — Dec 31) at current effective rates
- Burst pool: up to 40% above your historical baseline; overage billed at +10% per-token rate
- One-time reconciliation credit tiers applied after the 3-month window:
   * 0–20% overage: no credit

   * >40%: no credit, automatic exec review and possible conversion offer
- Conversion option: if Quantacore converts the burst into a new 12-month commit within 30 days of reconciliation, Redwood will apply a 3% conversion credit to the newly committed volume for the first year
- Invoice timing: reconciliation invoice generated within 10 business days of the window close; Net45 payment on true-up invoice

Attachments included: slim SOW amendment and redline (SOW-Quantacore-2028-redline.docx). DocuSign link to accept the amendment: https://redwood.app/docusign/XYZ123

Next steps: please review and let us know if procurement needs any specific invoice wording. If that looks good, sign via DocuSign and we'll route the SOW to Legal for final stamping.

Appreciate the partnership — want to make sure Quantacore can scale into the new product launch without disruption.

Best,
